speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of the lesion on your left dorsal hand, including its shape, color, and any associated symptoms like itching or pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the background. Is the lesion on your dorsal hand a new development, or has it been present for some time, and has it changed in size or appearance recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: The patient's description of a "rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque" on the dorsal hand is clinically inconsistent with a Urinary Tract Infection (UTI), which is an internal condition and does not present as a skin lesion. This presentation is highly suggestive of actinic keratosis or potentially squamous cell carcinoma given her age and sun exposure history. Please confirm if you have any other lesions or if this is an isolated finding on the hand.
